title: Chemical Coordination and Integration
syllabus: Endocrine glands and hormones; Human endocrine system - Hypothalamus, Pituitary, Pineal, Thyroid, Parathyroid, Thymus, Adrenal, Pancreas, Gonads; Hormones of heart, kidney, and gastrointestinal tract; Mechanism of hormone action; Role of hormones as messengers and regulators; Hypo- and hyperactivity and related disorders (Dwarfism, Acromegaly, Cretinism, Goiter, Exophthalmic goiter, Diabetes mellitus, Diabetes insipidus, Addison's disease).

questions.question: According to the modern scientific definition, hormones are non-nutrient chemicals that act as:
options: Intercellular messengers produced in trace amounts
Intracellular catalysts produced in large quantities
Nutrient reserves acting as direct sources of energy
Extracellular structural proteins forming cell junctions
questions.solution: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts by endocrine glands.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the hypothalamic hormones and their regulatory actions:

List-I (Hypothalamic Hormone)List-II (Target Action on Pituitary)
(A) Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)(I) Inhibits the release of Growth Hormone from anterior pituitary
(B) Somatostatin(II) Stimulates anterior pituitary to synthesize and release LH and FSH
(C) Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)(III) Stimulates anterior pituitary to secrete Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
(D) Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH)(IV) Stimulates anterior pituitary to secrete Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: GnRH stimulates the synthesis and release of gonadotropins (LH and FSH); Somatostatin inhibits the release of Growth Hormone; CRH stimulates ACTH secretion; TRH stimulates TSH secretion.

questions.question: The pituitary gland is lodged in a bony depression of the sphenoid bone called:
questions.solution: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella turcica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk (infundibulum).

questions.question: The anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) is regulated by the hypothalamus through ________, whereas the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) is under ________:
options: The hypophyseal portal system, direct neural regulation
Direct neural regulation, the hypophyseal portal system
questions.solution: The anterior pituitary is under the endocrine control of hypothalamic releasing/inhibiting hormones delivered via the hypophyseal portal circulatory system, whereas the posterior pituitary is under direct axonal/neural regulation of the hypothalamus.

questions.question: Hypersecretion of Growth Hormone (GH) in adults, particularly in middle age, causes severe disfigurement (especially of the face) and serious complications leading to premature death if unchecked. This clinical condition is called:
questions.solution: Over-secretion of GH in adults (after epiphyseal closure) leads to acromegaly, characterized by severe facial and limb disfigurement. Over-secretion in children leads to gigantism, and deficiency during childhood leads to pituitary dwarfism.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Pituitary hormones and their primary physiological functions:

List-I (Hormone)List-II (Major Function)
(A) Prolactin (PRL)(I) Stimulates powerful contraction of smooth muscles of uterus during childbirth
(B) Luteinizing Hormone (LH) in females(II) Regulates growth of mammary glands and milk synthesis
(C) Oxytocin(III) Induces ovulation of mature graafian follicle and maintains corpus luteum
(D) Vasopressin (ADH)(IV) Stimulates water and electrolyte reabsorption in DCT and collecting duct

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Prolactin: Regulates mammary development and lactation; LH in females: Induces ovulation and maintains corpus luteum; Oxytocin: Uterine contraction and milk ejection; Vasopressin (ADH): Water reabsorption in renal tubules.

questions.question: Which hormone is synthesized by the hypothalamus and transported axonally to the neurohypophysis (Pars nervosa) for storage and release?
questions.solution: Oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesized by the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to be stored and released from the neurohypophysis (Pars nervosa).

questions.question: Melatonin is secreted by the pineal gland. Which of the following is NOT a regulatory function of melatonin?
options: Stimulation of erythropoiesis in bone marrow directly
Maintenance of the 24-hour diurnal (circadian) sleep-wake cycle
Regulation of body temperature and metabolic rate
Influencing pigmentation, menstrual cycle, and immune defense capability
questions.solution: Melatonin regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm (sleep-wake cycle), body temperature, metabolism, skin pigmentation, menstrual cycle, and immune defense. Erythropoiesis is stimulated primarily by erythropoietin from the kidneys.

questions.question: The two lobes of the human thyroid gland are located on either side of the trachea and are interconnected by a thin flap of connective tissue called the:
questions.solution: The thyroid gland is composed of two lobes located on either side of the trachea. Both lobes are interconnected with a thin flap of connective tissue called the isthmus.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding disorders of the Thyroid Gland:

List-I (Disorder)List-II (Cause & Clinical Manifestation)
(A) Simple Goitre(I) Hypothyroidism in children causing stunted growth, mental retardation, and deaf-mutism
(B) Cretinism(II) Dietary iodine deficiency leading to enlargement of the thyroid gland
(C) Exophthalmic Goitre (Graves' disease)(III) Hyperthyroidism with enlarged gland, protruded eyeballs, increased BMR, and weight loss
(D) Myxedema(IV) Hypothyroidism in adults characterized by puffiness, lethargy, and low BMR

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Simple Goitre: Dietary deficiency of iodine; Cretinism: Congenital hypothyroidism causing stunted mental and physical growth; Graves' disease: Autoimmune hyperthyroidism with exophthalmos and elevated BMR; Myxedema: Adult hypothyroidism.

questions.question: Thyrocalcitonin (TCT), secreted by the parafollicular C-cells of the thyroid gland, is a peptide hormone that:
questions.solution: Thyrocalcitonin (TCT) lowers blood calcium levels (hypocalcemic effect) by inhibiting osteoclastic bone resorption and promoting calcium deposition into bone matrix.

questions.question: Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) increases blood $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ levels by which of the following mechanisms?
options: Stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption, increasing renal $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ reabsorption, and increasing intestinal absorption of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$
Inhibiting calcium absorption in the intestine
questions.solution: PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone that raises blood $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ by: (1) stimulating bone resorption (demineralization), (2) reabsorbing $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ from renal tubules, and (3) increasing intestinal absorption of dietary calcium via active Vitamin D.

questions.question: The thymus gland secretes peptide hormones called Thymosins. Thymosins play a major role in:
options: Differentiation of T-lymphocytes (cell-mediated immunity) and promoting antibody production (humoral immunity)
Controlling the secretion of thyroid hormones
questions.solution: Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity. In addition, thymosins promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity.

questions.question: Why does the immune response of old individuals become significantly weaker?
options: The thymus gland degenerates with age, resulting in reduced production of thymosins
The thyroid gland completely stops functioning
The parathyroid glands produce excessive calcitonin
The spleen stops producing red blood cells
questions.solution: The thymus is degenerated in old individuals resulting in a decreased production of thymosins. As a consequence, the immune responses of old persons become weak.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the histological zones of the Adrenal Cortex and their secreted corticosteroids:

List-I (Adrenal Cortical Zone)List-II (Secreted Hormone & Category)
(A) Zona glomerulosa (Outer layer)(I) Glucocorticoids (primarily Cortisol)
(B) Zona fasciculata (Middle layer)(II) Androgenic steroids (DHEA/Androstenedione)
(C) Zona reticularis (Inner layer)(III) Mineralocorticoids (primarily Aldosterone)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Zona glomerulosa (outer): Mineralocorticoids (Aldosterone); Zona fasciculata (middle): Glucocorticoids (Cortisol); Zona reticularis (inner): Androgenic corticosteroids.

questions.question: Adrenaline (Epinephrine) and Noradrenaline (Norepinephrine) are collectively called Catecholamines. During 'fight or flight' emergency conditions, catecholamines cause all of the following physiological responses EXCEPT:
options: Constriction of bronchioles and decreased heart rate
Pupillary dilation and piloerection (raising of hairs)
Increased heart rate, strength of heart contraction, and rate of respiration
Glycogenolysis in liver causing increased blood glucose levels
questions.solution: Emergency hormones (catecholamines) cause dilation of bronchioles (bronchodilation), pupil dilation, piloerection, increased heart rate/contractility, and stimulate glycogenolysis, lipolysis, and proteolysis. They do not constrict bronchioles or decrease heart rate.

questions.question: Cortisol is a major glucocorticoid that performs all of the following functions EXCEPT:
options: Stimulating cellular glucose uptake and utilization in peripheral tissues
Suppressing immune responses and producing anti-inflammatory reactions
Stimulating RBC production (erythropoiesis) and maintaining cardiovascular functions
questions.solution: Cortisol stimulates gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, proteolysis, and inhibits cellular uptake and utilization of amino acids and glucose (producing a hyperglycemic effect). It also produces anti-inflammatory effects, suppresses immunity, and supports erythropoiesis.

questions.question: Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules to stimulate:
options: Reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water, and excretion of $\text{K}^+$ and phosphate ions
Excretion of water and retention of hydrogen ions
questions.solution: Aldosterone acts mainly on the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct to stimulate active reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water, and excretion of $\text{K}^+$ and phosphate ions, maintaining electrolyte balance and blood pressure.

questions.question: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex alters carbohydrate metabolism, causing acute weakness, fatigue, hyperpigmentation of skin, and hypotension. This clinical condition is known as:
questions.solution: Underproduction of hormones (hypocortisolism and hypoaldosteronism) by the adrenal cortex alters carbohydrate and mineral metabolism, causing acute weakness, fatigue, nausea, skin bronze pigmentation, and low blood pressure, known as Addison's disease.

questions.question: The endocrine pancreas contains 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans. Glucagon is secreted by ________ and Insulin is secreted by ________:
questions.solution: The two main types of cells in the Islets of Langerhans are $\alpha$-cells which secrete Glucagon and $\beta$-cells which secrete Insulin.

questions.question: Glucagon is a peptide hormone that acts primarily on hepatocytes to stimulate:
options: Glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, resulting in hyperglycemia
Glycogenesis and lipogenesis, resulting in hypoglycemia
Glucose uptake by adipocytes and skeletal muscles
questions.solution: Glucagon is a hyperglycemic hormone that acts on hepatocytes to stimulate glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis while reducing cellular glucose uptake, thereby increasing blood glucose concentration.

questions.question: Insulin enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilization primarily by activating:
options: GLUT-4 glucose transporters in hepatocytes and adipocytes, and promoting glycogenesis
questions.solution: Insulin is a hypoglycemic hormone that enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilization (by translocating GLUT-4 transporters in muscle and adipocytes) and stimulates glycogenesis (conversion of glucose to glycogen) in hepatocytes.

questions.question: Prolonged hyperglycemia associated with loss of glucose in urine (glycosuria) and the formation of harmful breakdown products called ketone bodies (ketonuria) is diagnostic of:
questions.solution: Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to a complex disorder called Diabetes mellitus, which is associated with loss of glucose through urine (glycosuria) and formation of harmful breakdown products known as ketone bodies (ketonuria).

questions.question: Leydig cells (interstitial cells) present in the intertubular spaces of the human testis produce a group of hormones called androgens (mainly testosterone). Androgens play a role in:
options: Development of male secondary sexual characters, stimulation of spermatogenesis, and anabolic effects on protein metabolism
questions.solution: Androgens (testosterone) regulate the development, maturation, and functions of male accessory sex organs, stimulate spermatogenesis, influence male sexual behavior (libido), and exert anabolic effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.

questions.question: In the human ovary, Estrogen is synthesized and secreted mainly by ________, while Progesterone is secreted primarily by ________:
questions.solution: Estrogen is synthesized and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles. After ovulation, the ruptured follicle transforms into the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone.

questions.question: Progesterone supports pregnancy and acts on mammary glands to stimulate the:
options: Formation of alveoli (sac-like structures storing milk) and milk secretion
questions.solution: Progesterone supports pregnancy, prepares the endometrium for implantation, and acts on mammary glands to stimulate the development of alveoli (secretory sacs that store milk) and milk secretion.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding non-endocrine tissues and their secreted hormones:

List-I (Organ / Tissue)List-II (Secreted Hormone & Function)
(A) Atrial wall of heart(I) Erythropoietin (stimulates erythropoiesis in bone marrow)
(B) Juxtaglomerular cells of kidney(II) Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF - causes vasodilation to lower BP)
(C) Gastric mucosa(III) Gastrin (stimulates secretion of $\text{HCl}$ and pepsinogen)
(D) Duodenum / Pancreas(IV) Secretin and Cholecystokinin (CCK)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Atrial wall: ANF; JG cells of kidney: Erythropoietin; Gastric mucosa: Gastrin; Duodenum: Secretin (acts on exocrine pancreas to secrete water/bicarbonate) and CCK (stimulates pancreatic enzymes and bile release).

questions.question: Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on which of the following two target organs to stimulate their secretions?
questions.solution: CCK acts on both the exocrine pancreas (stimulating secretion of pancreatic digestive enzymes) and the gall bladder (stimulating contraction and release of bile juice into the duodenum).

questions.question: Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP) functions to:
questions.solution: Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP) inhibits gastric acid secretion and slows gastrointestinal motility.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the chemical nature of hormones:

List-I (Chemical Category)List-II (Hormone Examples)
(A) Peptide / Protein hormones(I) Cortisol, Testosterone, Estradiol, and Progesterone
(B) Steroid hormones(II) Epinephrine and Norepinephrine
(C) Iodothyronines(III) Insulin, Glucagon, Pituitary hormones, and Parathyroid hormone
(D) Amino-acid derivatives(IV) Thyroid hormones ($T_3$ and $T_4$)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Peptide/protein: Insulin, Glucagon, pituitary hormones, PTH; Steroids: Cortisol, Testosterone, Estradiol, Progesterone; Iodothyronines: $T_3, T_4$; Amino-acid derivatives: Epinephrine, Norepinephrine (derived from Tyrosine).

questions.question: Water-soluble peptide and protein hormones (e.g., FSH, Insulin) cannot pass through the lipid bilayer of target cell membranes. They exert their physiological action by:
options: Binding to membrane-bound receptors and generating intracellular second messengers (e.g., cyclic $\text{AMP}$, $\text{IP}_3$, $\text{Ca}^{2+}$)
Diffusing into the nucleus and binding to histone proteins directly
Directly altering chromosomal DNA without receptors
questions.solution: Water-soluble peptide hormones bind to membrane-bound extracellular receptors, which generates intracellular second messengers (such as $\text{cAMP}, \text{IP}_3, \text{Ca}^{2+}$) that regulate cellular metabolism via biochemical cascades.

questions.question: Lipid-soluble hormones like Steroid hormones (Estrogen, Progesterone, Cortisol) and Iodothyronines regulate target cell function by:
options: Crossing the cell membrane and binding to intracellular/nuclear receptors to regulate gene expression
Generating cyclic $\text{AMP}$ at the plasma membrane
Opening cell membrane sodium channels only
questions.solution: Lipid-soluble steroid hormones and thyroid hormones easily cross the plasma membrane and interact with intracellular receptors (mostly nuclear receptors). The hormone-receptor complex interacts with the genome to regulate gene expression and protein synthesis.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: FSH stimulates growth and development of ovarian follicles in females.
Statement II: In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from Leydig cells.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. FSH stimulates follicular growth in females and spermatogenesis in males (along with androgens). In males, LH is also called ICSH because it stimulates Leydig cells to produce androgens.

questions.question: Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) is secreted by which part of the pituitary gland and what is its primary function?
options: Pars intermedia; acts on melanocytes to regulate skin pigmentation
questions.solution: MSH is secreted by the Pars intermedia (which in humans is almost merged with the Pars distalis). MSH acts on melanocytes (melanin-containing cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin.

questions.question: A hormone that is an amino-acid derivative synthesized from the amino acid Tyrosine is:
questions.solution: Epinephrine, norepinephrine, and thyroid hormones are derived from the amino acid Tyrosine. Melatonin is derived from Tryptophan.

questions.question: Which of the following hormones is known as the 'birth hormone' and 'milk-ejection hormone'?
questions.solution: Oxytocin causes vigorous uterine contractions during parturition (birth hormone) and stimulates the contraction of myoepithelial cells around mammary alveoli for milk ejection (milk let-down hormone).

questions.question: Failure of the posterior pituitary to release adequate amounts of ADH (Vasopressin) leads to:
options: Excessive loss of water in urine resulting in dehydration (Diabetes insipidus)
questions.solution: An impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water, leading to water loss and dehydration. This condition is known as Diabetes insipidus.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of hormones are antagonistic in their physiological regulation of blood calcium levels?
questions.solution: PTH is hypercalcemic (increases blood $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ levels) while TCT is hypocalcemic (decreases blood $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ levels), acting as an antagonistic pair for calcium homeostasis.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of hormones are antagonistic in their regulation of blood glucose levels?
questions.solution: Insulin lowers blood glucose (hypoglycemic hormone), whereas Glucagon raises blood glucose (hyperglycemic hormone).

questions.question: Grave's disease (Exophthalmic goitre) is an autoimmune condition characterized by:
options: Hyperthyroidism, enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of the eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate, and weight loss
Hypothyroidism, stunted growth, and mental retardation
Hyposecretion of adrenal corticosteroids causing hypoglycemia
Excess secretion of parathyroid hormone causing bone softening
questions.solution: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterized by enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of the eyeballs (exophthalmos), increased basal metabolic rate (BMR), and weight loss.

questions.question: Erythropoietin (EPO), which stimulates the formation of RBCs (erythropoiesis) in bone marrow, is produced by the:
questions.solution: The juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney produce a peptide hormone called erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis (RBC formation) in the bone marrow.

questions.question: Which of the following endocrine glands is located on the dorsal side of the heart and aorta, and plays a role in the development of the immune system?
questions.solution: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta, responsible for maturation of T-lymphocytes.

questions.question: Secretin is a gastrointestinal peptide hormone that acts on the:
options: Exocrine pancreas to stimulate secretion of water and bicarbonate ions
Gallbladder to stimulate contraction and bile release
Stomach to stimulate secretion of pepsinogen
Salivary glands to stimulate amylase secretion
questions.solution: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates the secretion of water and bicarbonate ions to neutralize acidic chyme entering the duodenum.

questions.question: A female patient presents with abnormal growth of facial hair (hirsutism), deepening of voice, and menstrual irregularities. This condition (adrenal virilism) is caused by the hypersecretion of:
options: Androgenic corticoids from the Zona reticularis of the adrenal cortex
questions.solution: Hypersecretion of androgenic corticoids (male sex steroids) from the zona reticularis of the adrenal cortex in females leads to adrenal virilism (appearance of male secondary sexual traits like facial hair and voice changes).

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Insulin is a peptide hormone that lowers blood glucose by promoting cellular glucose uptake and glycogenesis.
Statement II: Glucagon is a peptide hormone that raises blood glucose by stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Insulin and glucagon operate antagonistically to maintain blood glucose homeostasis around normal levels ($80-120\text{ mg/dL}$).
